node.label: Time-pressed busy parents
node.summary: Parents who buy on time savings. They will pay if the tool clearly saves hours each week and cuts busywork.

node.summary: Buyers who already pay for many subscriptions. They resist $49/month and would pay a one-time price or accept a lower tier.

node.label: Incumbent-tied skeptics
node.summary: Users whose data and workflows sit in the incumbent product. They are reluctant to switch unless import and sync work cleanly.

node.label: Privacy-first evaluators
node.summary: Buyers who will not upload household data without a clear policy and export guarantees.

node.label: Group-chat recommenders
node.summary: Buyers who adopt products once peers vouch for them. Word of mouth drives their decisions.

node.label: Subscription fatigue
node.summary: Buyers see $49/month as one subscription too many and prefer one-time pricing.

node.label: Price above $49 is a dealbreaker
node.summary: Many posts say they would try the product only under $49, and they note the incumbent has a free tier.

node.label: Lock-in and sync with incumbent
node.summary: Switching cost is high because data and workflows are in the incumbent. Buyers want import and sync.

node.label: Data privacy and training concerns
node.summary: Buyers fear their household data will be used for training and want clear export and privacy policies.

node.label: Reliability over feature count
node.summary: Buyers say crashes and wrong outputs matter more than features. Demos that break on real use lose trust.

node.label: Long or hard onboarding
node.summary: Buyers abandon products whose setup takes more than about five minutes or has a steep learning curve.

node.label: Skepticism toward AI hype
node.summary: Buyers are tired of 'AI-powered' claims and doubt most AI product tools deliver.

node.label: Weak mobile and offline access
node.summary: Buyers do most tasks on phones and want offline function. Incumbent mobile apps are seen as weak.

node.label: Desire for time savings
node.summary: Strong positive intent: buyers say that a tool that saves hours or cuts busywork is an instant buy.

node.label: Rising subscription fatigue
node.summary: Coverage reports younger buyers are tiring of product app subscriptions and investors are cooling as consumer spending tightens.

node.label: AI hype fatigue
node.summary: Launches labelled AI-powered are increasingly met with scepticism. Startups race to add AI features anyway.

node.label: Backlash against incumbent data policy
node.summary: The incumbent faces backlash over training on user content, which opens space for privacy-first alternatives.

node.label: Rise of indie product tools
node.summary: Coverage notes indie tools challenging the incumbent.

node.label: Big incumbent product tool (unnamed)
node.summary: The dominant incumbent with a free tier and a broad feature set. Users complain about crashes, learning curve, mobile app, and a data policy change.

node.label: Indie product tools
node.summary: Smaller startups are gaining share against the incumbent as buyers look for simpler options.

node.label: General AI chatbots
node.summary: Buyers ask why they should not use a general chatbot directly, which frames a wrapper as a weak alternative.
